quality_checklist.overall_rationale: The study is a credible and relevant CubeSat MBSE/PLM case with explicit requirements-in-loop traceability and EPS power simulation evidence. Its main weaknesses are limited replicability detail, no shared models, and broad process/value claims that are supported mainly by one illustrative simulation rather than comparative or operational evidence.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Retained as supporting: the paper directly addresses CubeSat MBSE/RFLP requirements traceability and pre-physical EPS power verification, but the central contribution is an integrated PLM workflow rather than a broadly reusable nanosatellite EPS modeling framework.
bibliographic_review_management.citation: Rehman, M. U., & Fortin, C. (2024). An Implementation of Integrated Approach in Product Life-cycle Management Tool to Ensure Requirements-In-Loop During Complex Product Development: A Cubesat Case Study. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-031-62578-7_21.
bibliographic_review_management.title: An Implementation of Integrated Approach in Product Life-cycle Management Tool to Ensure Requirements-In-Loop During Complex Product Development: A Cubesat Case Study

RQ1.rationale: The paper models a CubeSat using RFLP, multiple viewpoints, SysML, and Dymola, but it does not present a minimal-knowledge modeling method; it requires numerical requirements, mission-planning data, and Dymola behavior models.

RQ2.rationale: It reports EPS-related power/SoC verification and claims improved requirements traceability and interoperability, but gives no explicit reliability or reproducibility metrics and no baseline or operational evidence.

RQ3.rationale: The core case integrates verification into requirements-linked Dymola simulations and DOE before physical development, with SoC and voltage checked against numerical requirements.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: This extraction should be synthesized as a requirements-in-loop/RFLP-in-PLM CubeSat case. It overlaps with traceability, PLM integration, and digital verification themes more than with detailed EPS hardware design.

toolchain_fragmentation_interoperability.rationale: The paper describes ENOVIA-CATIA-Dymola data flow and discusses closed PLM/domain-tool integration problems, but does not provide rigorous interoperability testing or standards implementation evidence.

lightweight_resource_constrained_tailori.rationale: CubeSat mass/power constraints motivate the battery case, but the MBSE process is not tailored for resource-constrained teams or lightweight implementation.

governance_project_deliverables_roi_valu.rationale: Decision support and requirements traceability are claimed, but governance mechanisms, deliverables, gates, and ROI/value metrics are not developed.

RQ1: A CubeSat can be represented using RFLP viewpoints in PLM, with requirements, functional/logical SysML architectures, physical links, and Dymola behavior models at decreasing abstraction levels.
The paper does not demonstrate minimal-knowledge modeling; it requires numerical requirement parameters, subsystem behavior models, and mission-planning/eclipse data.
The reported system boundary is the spacecraft after release/detumbling/stabilization, focused on an electrical-power viewpoint.
RQ2: EPS simulation showed SoC above 90% over 300 minutes against a 60% threshold and indicated the battery replenished to its initial value in the scenario.

Claimed process outcomes include requirements traceability, design decision support, configuration exploration, and improved interoperability, but evidence is mostly qualitative or single-case simulation.
Reliability and reproducibility outcomes are not quantified; model availability is not reported and the authors note degradation and closed-tool integration concerns.
RQ3: Verification is integrated by attaching numerical parameters to requirements and comparing Dymola simulation outputs with those parameters.
DOE explores candidate battery/EPS configurations; configurations failing requirements are treated as infeasible before physical development.
The digital test includes LEO/eclipse and power-profile inputs and produces voltage, SoC, and power plots used to assess EPS compliance.
